pyqgis_plugin.name: GIS Georgia Hub
pyqgis_plugin.description: One place in QGIS to browse, install and update the GIS GEORGIA plugins (catalog in Georgian and English).
pyqgis_plugin.about: GIS Georgia Hub is the catalog of the GIS GEORGIA plugins inside QGIS. Search the plugins, read what each one does and where to find it in QGIS, see its Processing algorithms and open them straight from the list, and install, update, disable or remove them with a click. Downloads come only from plugins.qgis.ge over HTTPS; the catalog is verified against a digital signature and every file against its SHA-256 checksum before anything is installed. On start-up the Hub can tell you when an update is available (it never updates by itself); it can also add the GIS GEORGIA repository to the QGIS Plugin Manager, but only if you say yes. Bilingual (ka/en). / GIS GEORGIA-ს დანამატების კატალოგი QGIS-ში: მოძებნე, ნახე რას აკეთებს და სად არის, გახსენი Processing-ის ალგორითმები, დააყენე ან განაახლე ერთი დაჭერით.

pyqgis_plugin.name: QGIS Environment Manager
pyqgis_plugin.description: What this QGIS is, which of your plugins declare support for QGIS 4, and what the GIS GEORGIA plugins need from the system (Georgian and English).
pyqgis_plugin.about: QGIS Environment Manager looks after the environment around QGIS. Diagnostics: version, release line (LTR or latest), Python, Qt, how QGIS was installed (on Linux: official repository, Flatpak, Snap, distribution), warnings such as an older-than-LTR version or the QGIS repository signing key that expires on 2027-08-08, and a report you can copy for support. Plugins and QGIS 4: reads each installed plugin's metadata.txt and shows what it declares for QGIS 3 and QGIS 4 (supportsQt6, minimum and maximum QGIS version), so you know what to check before moving to QGIS 4. Requirements: the GIS GEORGIA plugins that need system tools (PostgreSQL client tools and psycopg2 for PostGIS Manager, ExifTool for Photo Geotagger, SAGA and GRASS for GeoEco) are checked, and on Linux the missing ones can be installed with your package manager after you review the exact commands. Components: the programs and libraries around QGIS (GDAL, PROJ, GRASS, SAGA, Python libraries such as NumPy, pandas, Shapely, rasterio, database clients) with what is installed and what can be added, installed with your package manager after you review the commands - the small Linux form of the OSGeo4W chooser. What your plugins need (Plugins tab): reads the code of every installed plugin (never runs it) and lists the Python libraries it imports that the Python of this QGIS cannot import, with the system package for each and one-step install after you review the commands. A notice when QGIS starts (off by default, once a day, only if something needs attention). Doctor (Diagnostics tab): looks for what is known to break QGIS, through the Python that QGIS itself runs - your own copy of a Python library hiding the system one, GDAL tools and GDAL for Python of different versions, a bad PROJ path, a QGIS repository of another release, a half-finished package database, no free disk - and says what it could not look at. Environment file: write down which QGIS and which components a machine has and make other machines match (a class room, an office); the file holds only names from closed lists, never commands, and is checked before anything else. Safety: before anything is installed or changed the package manager is asked, in its own simulation mode, what it would do (how many packages, how much to download, whether something would be removed) and the answer is shown with the commands; before QGIS is changed in place a zip copy of your profile is made (only if that works), a copy can be restored as a new profile without touching the one in use, an installation can be taken back to another version the repositories offer, and a version can be kept so that updates skip it. Installed QGIS programs: every QGIS on the machine (system packages, Flatpak stable and lts, containers, Snap) with its version, a read-only check whether a newer build is waiting, and a way to start the one you pick after you see the command. QGIS versions: update the QGIS you have, or install another one next to it (Flatpak stable or lts, containers) or in its place - the program recommends the best way for your system and says why, shows every command first, and asks twice before changing the QGIS you are using right now; a zip copy of your profile can be made first. The logic is shared with the standalone qgis-installer (https://github.com/kapo-Toolkits/linux-scripts). Bilingual (ka/en). / QGIS-ის გარემოს მართვა: დიაგნოსტიკა, დანამატების თავსებადობა QGIS 4-თან და GIS GEORGIA-ს დანამატებისთვის საჭირო სისტემური ხელსაწყოები.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Plugin Downloader
pyqgis_plugin.description: Download all QGIS plugins into one folder, with progress and pause/resume.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Fetches the full plugin list from the official QGIS repository and downloads each plugin's latest stable ZIP into a folder you choose. Shows overall and per-file progress and supports pause / resume / stop. Bilingual EN/KA. The same code also runs as a standalone PyQt program.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Transliterate Data
pyqgis_plugin.description: Batch-transliterate Georgian names to clean Latin across a folder: shapefiles (+sidecars), database files (gpkg/sqlite/gdb), and inside them layers/feature classes and field names. Non-letter symbols become "_". Preview first, then apply in place or on a copy.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Point the plugin at a directory and it finds Georgian-named data and renames it to clean, filesystem- and SQL-safe Latin using the Georgian national romanization (lowercase, digraphs sh/ch/ts/gh/kh, no apostrophes); any other symbol becomes an underscore, with automatic collision handling (_2, _3). It renames: shapefile filesets (all sidecars together), database container files (.gpkg/.sqlite/.gdb), and — via GDAL/OGR — the layers/feature classes and field names inside GeoPackage, SQLite/Spatialite and Esri FileGDB. Always preview the old→new plan first; then apply in place, or work on a copy so the original is left untouched. Bilingual ka/en. Free/open-source, GPLv3.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Selection Tools
pyqgis_plugin.description: ArcGIS Pro-style "Selection" submenu on the layer context menu. Star tool: Make Layer From Selected Features — a new layer on the SAME source (no file written), saved with the project. Robust across GeoPackage, PostGIS, Shapefile and FileGDB.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Adds an ArcGIS Pro-like "Selection" submenu to the layer tree context menu: Zoom/Pan to selection, Clear, Switch, Select All, Select Visible Features, Generate Definition Query from Selection, Make Layer From Selected Features, and Attribute Table Showing Selection. "Make Layer From Selected Features" clones the layer (same data source URI — no .shp/.gpkg is written) and applies a definition query on the selected features; the query is stored in the project. Based on the idea of Murat Çalışkan's "Create Layer From Selected Features" (GPLv2+), reworked and improved by Giorgi Kapanadze: correct primary-key handling for PostGIS (gid/id) and FileGDB (OBJECTID) — not just "fid" — plus bilingual ka/en UI and the full ArcGIS-style submenu. See NOTICE.md for attribution. GPLv3.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Georgian Cadastre
pyqgis_plugin.description: Georgian cadastre toolkit for QGIS: fetch parcels by code from the public cadastre service, and prepare full cadastral survey drawings — UTM 37N/38N templates, WMS/WMTS services, name-based styles, Georgian fonts, an A4 layout with dynamic fields, an Excel attachment and a one-click packaged export.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Two tools in one bilingual (ka/en) plugin. (1) Cadastre fetch — enter a cadastral code (e.g. 38.10.42.107), search the public cadastre service and load the parcel: single, batch and bulk (radius / map extent) lookup, map-click reverse lookup, auto UTM zone 37N/38N, non-personal attributes, export to SHP/DXF/CSV. All network work runs on background tasks, proxy-aware, no login. (2) Cadastral Drawing — create the official "საკადასტრო აგეგმვითი/აზომვითი ნახაზი": download SHP templates (cadastre + floor-plan) in the right CRS, add WMS/WMTS orthophoto & cadastre services, apply symbology + labels automatically by layer name, download Georgian fonts, build an A4 print layout with dynamic date/area/CRS fields, fill the Excel attachment and package the PDF + Excel + photos into one folder named after the interested party. / ქართული კადასტრი + საკადასტრო აგეგმვითი/აზომვითი ნახაზის სრული ხელსაწყო.

pyqgis_plugin.name: PostGIS Manager
pyqgis_plugin.description: Unique spatial-database GIS toolkit for PostGIS — geometry editor on canvas, CRS audit, spatial join GUI, data-quality scoring, pgRouting network wizard, WFS, GPX import, thematic classification and snapshot diff. Not a pgAdmin clone.
pyqgis_plugin.about: PostGIS Manager is a hybrid QGIS plugin (3.40+ and 4.x) and standalone desktop app that fills the gap QGIS leaves in spatial database management — the "PostGIS as a GIS workspace" middle ground that neither QGIS nor pgAdmin covers well. Fully bilingual: English and Georgian (ქართული) with runtime switching. Light and Dark themes. Sidebar navigation (pgAdmin/DBeaver style).

pyqgis_plugin.name: DevBridge
pyqgis_plugin.description: Live PyQGIS debugging from QGIS: control panel with buttons for the VS Code (debugpy) and PyCharm bridges, one-click "prepare my plugin for debugging", and a bundled standalone desktop tool. Bilingual EN/KA.
pyqgis_plugin.about: DevBridge starts a debugpy server inside a running QGIS session so Visual Studio Code can attach and set breakpoints in plugin code or console scripts, without restarting QGIS; for PyCharm it detects your build, installs the matching pydevd-pycharm and connects. The Control Panel (Plugins > DevBridge) does everything with buttons, in English or Georgian: start/stop the bridges, pick one of your plugins and prepare it (a .venv that can import qgis, debugpy, VS Code launch configuration), open it in the file manager or VS Code. The same operations are also available as a separate desktop program bundled in the plugin's tool folder (launch it or open its folder from the panel); both share one settings file. Requires no extra Python packages except debugpy, which the preparation step installs.

pyqgis_plugin.name: GeoEco
pyqgis_plugin.description: Bilingual (ka/en) environmental toolkit — the "last mile" on top of SAGA/GRASS: solar PV energy & economics, wind resource & yield.
pyqgis_plugin.about: GeoEco does NOT reimplement solar/wind physics — it wraps existing open engines (SAGA "Potential Incoming Solar Radiation", GRASS r.sun, WindNinja) and adds the "last mile" they lack: energy (kWh), money (GEL), optimal PV tilt, wind resource & AEP, and bilingual (ka/en) reporting. First module: Energy (solar + wind). GPLv3.

pyqgis_plugin.name: Calculate Geometry
pyqgis_plugin.description: Guided dialog to populate one or more fields with geometry properties (coordinates, area, perimeter, length) — no expressions required.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Guided "Calculate Geometry" dialog: pick target field(s), a geometry property per field, a unit, and a CRS, then write the values in place. Built on existing QGIS core classes (QgsDistanceArea, QgsProjectionSelectionWidget, QgsUnitTypes). NOTE: early experimental release (v0.1.0) — not yet extensively tested. Upstream QGIS feature request: https://github.com/qgis/QGIS/issues/66902

pyqgis_plugin.name: Photo Geotagger
pyqgis_plugin.description: Writes GPS coordinates into photos (JPEG, TIFF, DNG; XMP sidecar for RAW and HEIC) from fixed or map-picked coordinates, a GPX track or a CSV table. Bilingual KA/EN; also runs as a standalone script.
pyqgis_plugin.about: Geotags JPEG photos from fixed or map-picked coordinates, a GPX track (by capture time) or a CSV table (by file name), and can add the photos to the project as a point layer. The core has no dependencies, so geotag.py also runs outside QGIS from the command line or a small window. Interface languages Georgian and English. License: GPL-3.0-or-later.
